messages:
maya: Ran an nsys trace on prod-sim for the short-chat workload after yesterday's batching tweak — hitrate on the prefix KV cache dropped ~12% and tail latency spiked for 50-200ms requests. Uploading trace. :confused:
perf-bot: Trace uploaded -> s3://redwood-traces/2141592653.nsys and perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/2141592653 (nsys+nvtx) :white_check_mark:
liam: :eyes: can you paste the exact config you used for the run? batch policy + kv settings?
maya: sure, minimal repro config I used:```json
{
  "batch_policy": "adaptive_v2",
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "batch_timeout_ms": 12,
  "kv_cache": {"mode": "prefix", "ttl_s": 300, "max_entries": 200000}
}
```
zara: we rolled adaptive_v2 yesterday in canary (rollout 2026-03-17). It merges short seqs more aggressively; I worry it coalesces different prefixes into the same batch which increases cache churn.
danielle: looking at the nsys timeline: attention kernels look fine, but there's a recurring pattern where "kv_lookup" kernels fire and immediately a large device memcpy happens (~1.2ms spikes) — suggests we evicted and reloaded KVs frequently. Short requests trigger many small lookups. snippet from timeline:```
[GPU] attention_forward 48%
[GPU] kv_lookup 20%
[Host->GPU memcpy] 8 peaks aligned with kv_lookup
[dispatcher] kernel_switch events cluster at t=12.3s
```
ben: could be prefix eviction policy interacting poorly with small batches. If adaptive_v2 groups requests, the running set of prefixes grows and we exceed max_entries, LRU kicks in. Do we have per-model partitioning enabled?
maya: per-model partitioning is enabled, but multi-tenant sim pushes multiple virtual models into the same pool. The cache size per-model is small in this test. I also saw more lock contention on the cache mutex in the host stacks (nvprof snapshot).
liam: nvprof output? even a few lines helps.
maya: nvprof shows host-side memcpy stalls correlated with cache miss bursts: ```
Frame 1234: memcpy H2D 1.18ms (spike)
Host CPU: cache_mutex_wait cumulative 42ms over 10s window
```
zara: ok this smells like two problems: (1) adaptive_v2 batch merging increases working set -> more evictions; (2) eviction + synchronous reload causes memcpy spikes and mutex contention. We can try: bump cache max_entries for the test, or make reload async.
danielle: another angle — kernel selection: when KV lookup misses we fall back to a slower fallback kernel path that does additional packing, adding ~0.6ms. The timeline shows fallback kernels sometimes chosen after the batching change. Might be kernel selector heuristics using sequence-length histogram; merging short sequences could change histogram and pick wrong kernel.
ben: good call. If kernel selector uses mean seq len and adaptive_v2 skews it, we might switch to a kernel optimized for longer tokens but slow on short. That + eviction is compounding.
liam: propose experiments (quick):
- repro with adaptive_v1 vs adaptive_v2 (same traffic)
- increase max_entries x2 for prefix cache
- enable async kv reload path
- force kernel selector to use short-seq path via override
Can someone run those in canary?
maya: running adaptive_v1 vs v2 now on canary A/B, bumping max_entries for a run too. Will attach traces. ETA ~30m.
perf-bot: Canaries started: canary-a(adaptive_v1, cache=200k) -> trace id 2141592660, canary-b(adaptive_v2, cache=400k) -> trace id 2141592670
zara: if canary-b (v2 + bigger cache) still shows memcpy spikes, we should prioritize async reload and a kernel selector guard to prevent falls when mean seq length fluctuates rapidly.
danielle: also add small-unit test for kernel selector with synthetic seq-length mixes, to catch this before rollouts.
ben: one quick mitigation: reduce batch_timeout_ms to 6ms so we form slightly smaller batches — might reduce working set size. Worth trying in the canary.
liam: thanks all. maya — post the traces and a short summary when done and we'll decide revert vs targeted fixes. :thumbsup:
maya: Will do. initial canary numbers look promising when cache doubled, hitrate recovered ~7% but memcpy spikes still present on some windows. Uploading next trace.```
